about: Bowed low, with his joined hands resting on the altar, the priest asks God that the offering be carried by the hands of His holy Angel to the altar on high before the divine majesty. The prayer does not name the Angel. The clause beginning with “ut” leads to “repleámur”: those who receive the Body and Blood of Christ ask to be filled with every blessing and grace.

s01.narrative: The priest bows low and lays his joined hands upon the altar.

s02.translation: In humble prayer we ask You, almighty God: command that these gifts be borne by the hands of Your holy Angel to Your altar on high, in the sight of Your divine majesty:

s04.translation: so that all of us, who

s11.translation: through this participation at the altar receive the most holy Body and Blood of Your Son

s05.narrative: The priest joins his hands and signs the cross once over the Host and once over the chalice.

s08.translation: may be filled with every grace and heavenly blessing.

s10.translation: Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

w001.function: An adjective referring to those who pray: “we, the suppliants”. The translation renders it adverbially as “humbly”.

w007.function: An accusative neuter plural: the subject of the infinitive “perférri” (w008).

w008.function: Present passive infinitive of “pérfero”: “to be carried”.

w012.function: Singular: one unnamed angel. The prayer does not identify him.

w023.function: Introduces the clause whose verb is “repleámur” (w041). An extended relative clause stands between the conjunction and its verb.

w024.function: Nominative plural, serving as the subject of “sumpsérimus” (w035).

w029.function: Agrees with “Corpus” (w032), which follows after the rubric: “the most holy Body”.

w035.function: The form can be a future perfect or a perfect subjunctive. The translation follows the first analysis: “shall receive”.

w040.function: An ablative with “repleámur” (w041): that with which one is filled.
